title: Playtest frame metrics and grouped rendering workload
context: Owner reported slowdown near wave 42 and suspected numerous ray towers. Existing optional FPS overlay had aggregate render counts, but no grouped workload or retained wave samples; clamped simulation dt could hide frame rates below 10 FPS.
outcome: Enable the compact FPS overlay by default unless the player has disabled it; backtick and the existing tuning switch still toggle it. FPS uses unclamped real frame intervals. Expand workload for enemy count, measured enemy/tower/game-frame CPU times, total GPU time when available and a descending batch inventory by Sentry family, tank, Terraformer, enemies, portals, beams/lightning, projectiles, debris, shield and remaining world. Counts are estimates before culling, not per-item GPU timings, and omit shader/overdraw pricing. Inventory is cached for two seconds. Samples are recorded every five seconds in bounded local diagnostics; Copy performance shares a short human-readable snapshot with selected-text fallback. GPU queries are capped at eight, reject disjoint measurements and release pending queries on toggle/disposal. Overlay follows the HUD lower edge.
alternatives: Do not attribute slowdown to Relay or Lancer without runtime measurements.
Per-draw GPU queries would add cost and can misrepresent tiled rendering; retain total GPU timing and explicitly labeled geometry estimates.
evidence: test/render-workload.mjs covers instancing, draw ranges, inherited visibility and no duplicate counts across category roots.
Browser --shield-perf verifies the expanded Relay row, persistent open state, actual clipboard copy and recorded performance samples.
npm test: 73 programs; npm run check; npm run test:browser; npm run build.
